pages.text: "All done!" Lolo in yellow boots popped a toothbrush into their mouth, then spat it out. Steam rose from the yard basin. In the winter night, Lolo's breath spread white.
"First one under the covers wins!" Lolo ran into the house. Behind, Riri in her yellow hat called, "What about between your teeth?" Lolo pretended not to hear and jumped over the threshold.
Under the covers, something tickled between Lolo's teeth. Pushing with a tongue did not loosen it; it kept catching. "Something is there..." Lolo touched a cheek and opened their eyes.
Mom came with a lamp. The window lamp was still lit. "Can you open wide and say ah?" Mom held a little mirror in front of Lolo.
Silver flashed between the teeth in the mirror. A fish scale from dinner was stuck there. "That was tickling me?" Lolo drew a sharp breath.
"You have watched Dad tending the net, right?" Mom whispered. "He cleans every little space between the threads. Brush, brush—even between your teeth!" Lolo threw back the covers and sprang up.
By the yard basin, Lolo gripped the toothbrush. Brush up, brush down! Gently between the teeth too, like cleaning the spaces in a net. Pop—the scale fell out.
Lolo rinsed and said, "Ah—" The teeth felt squeaky clean. The tickly spot was clear. Excited, Lolo splashed into the water with those boots.
Riri stood beside Lolo with her toothbrush. "One, brush up! Two, brush down! Three, gently between the teeth!" The next night, Lolo ran to the basin first.
Under the covers, Mom rubbed her cheek against Lolo's. Brushing between the teeth left nothing to tickle all night. "Brush, brush—even between your teeth!" Lolo showed a wide, toothy smile.
